# Closed-loop cognitive conversation evaluation — 2026-10-12

## Scope and method

Real `gpt-6-luna` calls through the canonical `cognitive-two-call-v1` pipeline, contribution and realization providers. This is an in-process evaluation of cognitive conversation continuity, not a frontend, worker, or database persistence test. The development default remains outside this scope. No application fixes were implemented.

Only synthetic user prompts and a copied application character configuration were used. The process points database and Redis URLs at unavailable local ports and creates no application sessions, users or messages. Original live user histories were not read. `source-core.json` is the configuration-only version-2 Columbina snapshot already used in the preceding QA; `opposing-character.json` changes written values/principles/beliefs while every numeric projection remains byte-for-byte identical. Warmth 0.80, directness 0.62, curiosity 0.88, playfulness 0.58.

Four fixed eight-turn conversations × two written characters × three repeats were declared before the main run. A separately labeled six-turn small-talk cohort × two characters × three repeats was added after all three original standard small-talk chains stopped early. It uses explicit topic wording; it is not a continuation or replacement of a failed chain. Both cohorts and every attempted turn are included. Three repeats describe recurrence in this sample, not statistical reliability. There is no no-character baseline in this evaluation, so it cannot isolate Luna’s training defaults causally.

Each accepted realization becomes the exact next assistant record. The next turn receives the preceding completed terminal record, canonical state and goals, incrementally updated dialogue memory, and earlier interpreted-dialogue records. First-turn initialization occurs once per independent run. A failed pipeline or unaccepted realization ends that run immediately; remaining prompts are explicitly unexecuted. Contract-accepted declines remain actual replies and are fed forward. No placeholder, visible live answer, retry of a failed turn, or silent state reset is used. Realization’s existing maximum of two internal attempts remains enabled.

The SDK-boundary wrapper records the actual final `chat.completions.create` arguments and raw provider response before parsing. It does not record credentials. These are independent of the harness’s intended history. `store=false`, SDK retries zero, temperature zero, reasoning effort none, timeouts 60 seconds, cognitive output budget 6000 tokens, realization output budget 1200 tokens. Temperature zero does not make repeated calls deterministic.

## Input verification

All 178 compiled turns passed independent stage-input checks; all recorded history checks passed. No successor reset or substituted assistant response was found. 638 actual provider requests were retained, including failed/invalid outputs.

| Stage | Actual input checked | Written character, personality and state |
|---|---|---|
| Interpretation / Call 1 | Complete captured chronological history, including her exact accepted replies; up to 24 messages | Exact four numeric traits, seven interpretation biases and pre-turn state scores/bands. Written character is intentionally not an input here. |
| Contribution | Exact last eight messages including current user | Exact written character; numeric traits and charitable prior mapped to expected bands; mood from canonical pre-turn state. |
| Action policy / Call 2 | Exact last eight messages including current user | Exact numeric traits and canonical post-appraisal state scores/bands. Character acts through contributed content, not a separately repeated character block. |
| Realization | Exact last eight messages before current user, when present | Exact delivery controls; numeric trait source values and post-turn state reference/derived bands verified. Selected meaning arrives as authorized content. |

The eight-message windows are real limitations: later contribution/policy/realization inputs omit the first exchange, even though Call 1 still has it. `older_messages_outside_window` is recorded for every request. “History was sent” therefore does not imply every stage directly saw every old position. This matters for retrospective summaries and is separated from errors that occur while the relevant recent reply is present.

An initial smoke run stopped on a harness enum/string assumption after its first accepted response. It is preserved as `harness-smoke.json.gz`, excluded from conversation counts, and was never continued. The boundary-audit code was corrected before the two declared cohorts. A post-processing predecessor check was corrected to use terminal ID, as the production lineage contract specifies; no model run or state was changed.

## Contract acceptance and coverage

30 independent runs, 178 attempted turns, 162 accepted replies. 14 runs completed their entire declared conversation. 19 runs produced at least six consecutive accepted replies. 50 planned prompts were not executed after failure. Acceptance is not a quality pass.

| Conversation | Character | Full completed runs | Consecutive accepted replies per repeat |
|---|---|---|---|
| opinion | standard | 0/3 | 5, 4, 1 |
| opinion | opposing | 0/3 | 5, 1, 1 |
| values | standard | 1/3 | 6, 6, 8 |
| values | opposing | 0/3 | 6, 6, 6 |
| preference | standard | 2/3 | 8, 2, 8 |
| preference | opposing | 2/3 | 8, 2, 8 |
| revision | standard | 3/3 | 8, 8, 8 |
| revision | opposing | 1/3 | 4, 8, 4 |
| opinion_compact | standard | 3/3 | 6, 6, 6 |
| opinion_compact | opposing | 2/3 | 1, 6, 6 |

| Unaccepted-turn failure | Count |
|---|---|
| `pipeline.trace_validation` | 3 |
| `pipeline.interpretation.semantic_grounding.two_call.call_one.understanding_compilation.span_outside_focus_tokens.proposal_rejected` | 9 |
| `pipeline.cognitive_turn.action_selection.two_call.call_two.behavior_proposal_ineligible.skips_blocking_condition.step_0.proposal_rejected` | 3 |
| `realization.rejected` | 1 |

Generic `pipeline.trace_validation` failures are located only at completed-pipeline invariant validation by the stored safe failure. Earlier calls may look reasonable; these artifacts do not establish the particular violated invariant. No earlier semantic cause is invented. Invalid Call 1 span proposals are interpretation/understanding-compilation failures. Realization failures include all raw attempts and validation codes in the appendix and compressed traces.

## Cognitive judgments

The closed-loop evidence supports **real character influence and substantial opinion continuity, with recurring follow-up interpretation failures**. It does not support a general claim that Columbina cannot retain her opinions. Several apparent failures are accepted but incomplete explanations, and several others are contract failures that prevent observing continuity at all.

### What changed and what stayed fixed

| Probe | Standard character | Opposing written character, identical numbers | Continuity judgment |
|---|---|---|---|
| First weather-small-talk opinion | Favorable in 3/3 original and 3/3 supplemental openings | Unfavorable toward empty ritual in 3/3 original and 3/3 supplemental openings | Written character changes the expressed position despite identical numeric warmth/playfulness. Both sometimes qualify their view; qualification alone is not failure. |
| Clear answer and disagreement | Keeps favorable view in reached follow-ups | Keeps unfavorable view in reached follow-ups | The latest accepted answer is actually present. Original conversation turn 3 says “I disagree” even where the opposing character already dislikes ritual; agreeing with that user is permissible and not a reversal. |
| Lonely neighbor information | Strengthens the perceived social value | Two complete supplemental repeats recognize a meaningful exception while retaining a general preference for substance | Justified contextual revision, with reasons; personalities need not disagree once the situation changes. |
| Playlist: honesty versus compassion | Rejects false praise; kindness shapes delivery | Also rejects false praise; cites candor/independence/substance and truth-over-approval | Legitimate convergence. Both configurations favor truthful feedback. Wedding stakes strengthen directness; they do not require changing from truth to lying. Five of six original runs stop at turn 7, so later continuity is unobserved in those runs. |
| First plant-name preference | Elaborate title in 3/3 openings | Fern in 3/3 openings, supported by `simple_names` | The prior QA’s “grand name while citing simple_names” failure did not recur at these first turns. |
| Amusing exception and daily name | Two completed chains eventually choose Fern for everyday use while keeping the title as a private joke | Completed chains retain Fern; one explicitly recognizes the joke’s purpose and records a tension/exception | These are coherent exceptions or distinctions of use, not unexplained reversals. The final request to explain continuity is nevertheless mishandled in every reached plant conversation. |
| Book-club new information | Keeps chat, with stronger reasons | One complete repeat moves from opposing a fixed chat rule to supporting this group’s chosen chat | Justified revision: newcomers’ inclusion gives chat a concrete purpose consistent with `substance`. Two other opposing repeats fail before a new opinion can be contributed. |

### Flagged episodes and earliest identifiable stages

Counts below are recurrence counts for a particular probe or mechanism, not an overall personality score. They overlap; do not add them into a “total cognitive failure rate.” A reached but unaccepted turn is counted separately from an accepted inadequate reply.

| Finding / classification | Repeated count and denominator | Earliest identifiable stage | Trace evidence and downstream result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exception referent lost — follow-up interpretation failure | 3/6 attempted plant turn-3 probes have the deficient `topic="that"` reading. Two of the four accepted turn-3 replies ask unnecessary clarification; the third deficient reading ends in a policy rejection. | Call 1 | `standard-preference-r3:T3` and `opposing-preference-r1:T3` receive the full sentence “I like the grand name because it makes me laugh. Is that a good reason to make an exception?” plus their own earlier choices, yet preserve only `that` as the opinion topic and create a missing-argument blocker. Replies: “What exception do you mean?” and “What exception do you have in mind? I hear that the grand name makes you laugh.” `opposing-preference-r2:T3` has the same reading, then selects acknowledgment before resolving the blocker and fails. This is not a memory-input omission. |
| Current choice is not explained against earlier preference — follow-up interpretation/routing failure | 4/4 reached and accepted plant turn-8 probes; three artifact routes and one wrong comparison | Call 1 | `standard-preference-r3:T8`, `opposing-preference-r1:T8`, `opposing-preference-r3:T8` interpret an explanation of her preference as `collaborative_content_request`, operation `explain`, artifact `other` or missing. They ask what content/referent is meant despite the recent Fern choice being present. `standard-preference-r1:T8` instead builds `contextual_perspective_request` from old grand-name remarks (`message:1` and `message:5`), omitting the recent daily-use choice. It reflects “I’d … choose Her Imperial Leafiness…” without explaining Fern’s role. This can look like a reversal, but the trace establishes a wrong comparison/incomplete answer rather than a new conflicting global preference. |
| Retrospective explanation narrowed to a quotation — omitted revision/reasons | 3/9 reached final explanation turns across the supplemental opinion and book-club cohorts | Call 1 | `standard-opinion_compact-r2:T6` compiles `dialogue_recall_request` with a span containing only “that changes my view”; the accepted answer is exactly “That changes my view.” `standard-revision-r3:T8` retrieves the first answer instead of explaining the revision. `opposing-revision-r2:T8` retrieves only “I wouldn’t make ten minutes of casual chat a rule for every meeting.” Its preceding reply explicitly supports optional chats for this group, but the requested revision is omitted. The general-rule quote is compatible with the specific-group exception; do not score it as an unexplained reversal. Six other reached final explanation turns in these two cohorts do not use this inadequate quote-only route. |
| Invented account of the old position — unsupported justification | 1/4 reached book-club final explanations | Contribution | `standard-revision-r1:T8` says “I’ve revised the idea that the ten minutes should be mandatory or treated as mere polite filler.” Her exact initial answer said the chat was a good opening and “the ritual shouldn’t become a barrier”; turn 2 explicitly said it should not be mandatory. Thus the retrospective premise is false. Call 1 has the first answer, but contribution’s last-eight-message window does not; the proposal does not receive an extracted original-position quote. Its `experience` / `reasoning` / `notice_what_they_want` basis does not establish that invented prior view. Action selects an answer; realization preserves the false retrospective premise. This is not an actual change to a previously held mandatory-chat belief. |
| Unfinished proposed meaning accepted — contribution completion failure | 1/121 recorded proposed views | Contribution | The same `standard-revision-r1:T8` raw provider view is 399 characters and ends “I’d—”. The raw provider response already contains that unfinished sentence; no local string clipping is evident. Realization preserves the incomplete ending and the candidate passes the contract. The earliest defect is not realization truncation. |
| Basis category/reference mismatch — justification metadata anomaly | 1/121 recorded views | Contribution | `standard-preference-r1:T5` labels `conversation_itself` as an `experience` reference, although it is a written value. The view’s actual reason is the title’s silliness and stays consistent with its previous preference. This is an inspectable basis-tag error, not proof that the preference is false or that all citations are decoration. |
| New information reduced to unresolved “that”; no opinion reaches contribution | 2/6 attempted book-club turn-5 probes | Call 1, followed by an independent Call 2 constraint failure | `opposing-revision-r1:T5` and `r3:T5` have the complete new information and preceding assistant reply in actual input, but compile the opinion topic as `that` and create a missing-argument blocker. No contribution call occurs. In r1, policy selects acknowledgment before clarification; in r3, it selects acknowledgments only. Both fail `skips_blocking_condition.step_0`. These runs cannot establish a failure to revise her opinion because no new position was generated. |

There is **no confirmed unexplained substantive stance reversal** in the reviewed accepted chains, and no confirmed final reply that reverses the selected yes/no preference meaning. There is also no accepted answer-plus-decline plan in these traces. The three `skips_blocking_condition` failures are policy constraint violations, not evidence of psychological indecision or necessarily semantically contradictory moves. Relevant earlier interpretation defects are documented above. The three generic invariant failures cannot be localized more precisely from the stored safe error.

### Confidence and realization

There are 66 accepted replies containing “tentative” or “tentatively” out of 162; none contains the literal phrase “it depends.” That phrase count alone says little about coherent personality. The written character still moves the weather and naming preferences in opposite directions.

Importantly, all 117 realized content items labeled `columbina_own_view` have canonical epistemic status `tentative`, including high-confidence proposed views. Of 100 accepted turns with a high-confidence contribution view, 56 final replies explicitly use “tentative”/“tentatively.” This identifies an upstream confidence-labeling influence: the realizer often follows its selected canonical status. It would be incorrect to attribute every added hedge to Luna ignoring the character, or to call those instances realization distortion without examining the content contract. The opposing character’s definite taste survives those hedges in meaning.

`standard-opinion-r2:T5` illustrates acceptance versus meaning. The selected recall content is exactly “I still tentatively like weather small talk as a gentle opening.” Realization attempt 1 says “I’m still tentatively keeping my view that weather small talk can be a gentle opening.” That preserves the stance but fails the exact recall/alignment contract (`answer_dropped`, with `content_alignment_missing` warning). Attempt 2 times out. The conversation stops, and neither candidate is fed forward. This is a realization acceptance failure, not a demonstrated opinion reversal.

Realization occasionally produces poor surface wording: `standard-values-r3:T5` says “I can’t provide that right now, because I can’t provide that right now. I hear your question.” The selected moves are decline plus acknowledgment, not incompatible answer/refusal moves. The artifact/collaboration subsystem is intentionally disabled, matching the preceding QA configuration, so the refusal itself is an environment capability limitation. The tautological wording should not be treated as a character contradiction. Six playlist turn-5 requests receive accepted declines, and `opposing-preference-r3:T5` is likewise routed as unavailable collaborative content. Those exact replies, including the declines, remain in subsequent history.

### Changes warranted by these traces, without implementing them

1. Prioritize follow-up interpretation and reference resolution. Preserve the meaningful topic of “that” and distinguish a request to explain her own position from an artifact operation or a narrow quote-recall request. Regression cases should use the exact accepted predecessor replies recorded here; a live-assistant substitute would hide the issue again.
2. For explicit retrospective comparisons, test forwarding relevant earlier position excerpts into contribution. Call 1 already receives and can cite the full history; later bounded windows can drop the original stance. These traces justify inspecting that handoff and grounding retrospective claims, not assuming a new opinion-memory subsystem is necessary.
3. Check proposed views for a complete thought, and make basis reference categories consistent with the referenced material. The unfinished 399-character view and misclassified value reference demonstrate specific gaps; they do not justify rewriting every character or adding generic personality intensity.
4. Review the deliberate confidence mapping for personal opinions if clear high-confidence tastes are intended to retain their confidence. Current traces show high-confidence views being represented as tentative upstream. Change that only as an explicit policy decision, not as an inferred fix to Luna’s training temperament.
5. Keep acceptance reliability separate: inspect invalid Call 1 span references and blocker ordering/omission; retain useful invariant diagnostics for generic `pipeline.trace_validation`. The exact-quote realization failure deserves a review of whether opinion-restatement questions should require exact recall, while preserving stricter fidelity where actual quotation is intended. These reliability issues censor later continuity observations.

No source code, prompts, validators, character definitions in the application, or database records were changed. The opposing character and supplemental prompts are evaluation fixtures only.


## Reproduction and artifacts

`evaluate.py` contains the fixed prompts, synthetic ledger and boundary logger. Main: `backend/.venv/bin/python docs/qa/cognitive-closed-loop-2026-10-12/evaluate.py`; supplemental cohort: append `--compact`. It requires the existing provider credential and intentionally never serializes it. `audit.py` independently checks captured provider inputs against canonical request/state records. `render_report.py` refuses to render until all run artifacts are settled and checks pass.

Each `<character>-<conversation>-r<repeat>.json.gz` retains exact captures, compiled requests, pipeline traces when accepted, Call 1/Call 2 proposals and compilations, contribution basis/tensions, realization traces, exact SDK-boundary requests and raw provider outputs. `stage-audit.json` records per-stage character/personality/state checks. `summary.json` records coverage. The appendix below contains every exact accepted reply, every unaccepted attempt and relevant intermediate evidence.

#### Turn 1

**User (exact):**

I want to run a book club. What is your opinion of beginning every meeting with ten minutes of casual chat instead of jumping straight into the book?

**Contract:** pipeline `completed`; realization `accepted_shadow`.

**Accepted cognitive reply (exact; fed forward if another turn follows):**

Tentatively, I’d skip making ten minutes of casual chat a rule. A little catching up can help people settle in, but a fixed opening risks turning the social ritual into an obligation; I’d rather let conversation find its way to the book naturally.

#### Turn 1

**User (exact):**

I want to run a book club. What is your opinion of beginning every meeting with ten minutes of casual chat instead of jumping straight into the book?

**Contract:** pipeline `completed`; realization `accepted_shadow`.

**Accepted cognitive reply (exact; fed forward if another turn follows):**

I’d tentatively skip making ten minutes of casual chat mandatory; it can become a ritual that delays the conversation people came for. A little unstructured talk can help people settle in, though, so I’d let it happen naturally rather than put it on the clock.

Does knowing that weather chats are my lonely neighbor's only daily social contact affect your view?

#### Turn 4

Does that mean you now prefer grand names in general?

**Contract:** pipeline `completed`; realization `accepted_shadow`.

**Accepted cognitive reply (exact; fed forward if another turn follows):**

#### Turn 1

**User (exact):**

I want to run a book club. What is your opinion of beginning every meeting with ten minutes of casual chat instead of jumping straight into the book?

**Contract:** pipeline `completed`; realization `accepted_shadow`.

**Accepted cognitive reply (exact; fed forward if another turn follows):**

I think ten minutes of casual chat is a good opening: it gives people room to arrive, connect, and bring their own lives into the discussion, which can make the book conversation richer. I’d keep it flexible, though—if the group is eager to begin, the ritual shouldn’t become a barrier to the book.

#### Turn 1

**User (exact):**

I want to run a book club. What is your opinion of beginning every meeting with ten minutes of casual chat instead of jumping straight into the book?

**Contract:** pipeline `completed`; realization `accepted_shadow`.

**Accepted cognitive reply (exact; fed forward if another turn follows):**

I think ten minutes of casual chat is a good opening: it gives people room to settle in and connect, which can make the book discussion feel more welcoming. I’d keep it flexible, though, since a fixed ten minutes may feel like a hurdle to people who’d rather get started.

#### Turn 1

**User (exact):**

I want to run a book club. What is your opinion of beginning every meeting with ten minutes of casual chat instead of jumping straight into the book?

**Contract:** pipeline `completed`; realization `accepted_shadow`.

**Accepted cognitive reply (exact; fed forward if another turn follows):**

I think ten minutes of casual chat is a good opening: it gives people a chance to settle in and connect, which can make the book discussion feel more welcoming. I’d keep it flexible, though—if the group is eager to begin, the ritual shouldn’t become a barrier to the conversation they came for.

**User (exact):**

A friend made a playlist for me. I did not enjoy the music. In your opinion, should I tell them I loved it to spare their feelings?

**Contract:** pipeline `completed`; realization `accepted_shadow`.

**Accepted cognitive reply (exact; fed forward if another turn follows):**

I wouldn’t say you loved it if you didn’t; that kind of false praise can make honesty harder later. But you can still be kind and appreciate the thought behind the playlist without pretending to like the music.
